purpose: Every immersive gameplay/media mechanic must be validated independently before MonIA can treat it as production-ready.
global_rule: No mechanic becomes live-canonical merely because one generated clip looks good. Each mechanic is tested against identity, camera grammar, performance, continuity, player agency and technical reliability.

character_reference_policy.rule: User-supplied Lucas references may teach identity, body, movement, voice, gaze, intimacy/performance vocabulary and everyday behavior. They do not dictate story events.
lucas_reference_dimensions: underwear / morning / bed context when non-explicit and appropriate

visio_incoming.goal: Lucas unexpectedly calls Marion and the result feels like a real live video call rather than a cinematic clip.
must_pass: viewer is Lucas phone front camera
phone itself is invisible
Lucas mostly looks toward Marion's on-screen image with brief natural lens checks
gaze is not persistently off to one side
natural listening state before/after speech
V16 voice identity
speech/mouth coherence
natural breathing, blinks, micro-movement and handheld drift
context-appropriate wardrobe/location/light
incoming-call surprise presentation integrates with gameplay

visio_outgoing.goal: Marion calls Lucas and Lucas answers according to his real current context/availability.
must_pass: answer can vary by context
Lucas may be busy, moving, tired, at home, outdoors or between activities
same front-camera grammar as incoming visio
gaze reads as interaction with Marion rather than generic performance
V16 speaking coherence
transition from call UI to live feed is believable

desktop_tablet_choice_scene.goal: A living full-screen scene continues while discreet choices or free action appear.
must_pass: scene remains visually alive while player decides
choices do not dominate the screen
free-response or free-action path exists where appropriate
POV remains default unless cinematic grammar is intentionally invoked
choice result returns cleanly into the world

pov_gameplay.goal: Player experiences ordinary life through Marion's viewpoint without constantly seeing Marion.
must_pass: world feels inhabited rather than static
Lucas behaves spatially in the scene when present
ambient motion does not trigger unnecessary cutscenes
mini-phone remains accessible without becoming the main interface
camera feels appropriate for desktop/tablet

external_cinematic.goal: Camera leaves Marion's POV only when seeing Marion materially improves the moment.
must_pass: Marion and Lucas identities stay canonical across shots
camera grammar is cinematic, not visio/selfie
relationship and physical continuity are correct
player agency is preserved at consequential decisions
return to POV/gameplay is natural

long_cinematic_60_120s.goal: MonIA can create one- to two-minute scenes by assembling validated short shots without identity drift.
must_pass: same Lucas and Marion throughout
wardrobe/hair/light/location continuity
dialogue continuity
screen-direction continuity
voice identity continuity
failed shot can be regenerated without rebuilding entire sequence

private_daily_life.goal: MonIA can create believable private everyday moments such as waking up, getting dressed, lying in bed, quiet home behavior or close affectionate interaction.
must_pass: Lucas body and face remain canonical
body proportions stay stable
tattoos are correct when visible
wardrobe state fits context
non-explicit intimacy stays natural rather than posed
movement resembles approved private-home references rather than generic model motion

whisper_close_proximity.goal: Close tender or whispered interaction feels physically believable and emotionally restrained.
must_pass: mouth/head proximity is anatomically credible
whisper performance matches intended voice behavior
no exaggerated romance posing
camera distance fits either POV or cinematic grammar
identity stays stable at close range

promotion_rule: Only explicit user validation or a clearly recorded project decision may move a mechanic to approved-mechanic.

visio_gaze_rule.target: Lucas should visually read as attending to Marion on the screen, not staring permanently into the lens and not looking persistently off-axis.
acceptable_behavior: mostly screen-focused gaze near camera axis
brief natural glances away for thought/context
reject: eyes that do not react to conversation
